name: Printing Consecutive Numbers Within a Specified Range (Case 1)
description: Construct a program that prints a sequence of numbers from 1 (inclusive) to 9 (inclusive).

comments.content:
We need to repeat printing the numbers that are in a sequence from 1 (inclusive) to 9 (inclusive). To do this, we need to use a loop structure. We use for loops instead of a while loop because we need to repeat the loop 9 times, and for loops are best-suited in cases like this when we know ahead of time the number of times that we need to repeat the loop. Here, we want the for loop to start counting from 1 with every integer number up to (including) 9.

To do this, we initialize variable num to 1, loop until reaching 9 (inclusive), and increment num by 1 after each iteration of the loop.

In the first part of the loop header, we define a control variable num and initialize it to 1. In the second part of the loop header, we test whether the control variable has reached the termination threshold. The loop is repeated if the control variable is less than or equal to 9 and terminates when the control variable reaches 10. In the third part of the loop header, we increment the control variable by 1 after each iteration of the loop.

Note that the first part is executed once before the loop starts, the second part is executed before each iteration, and the third part is executed after each iteration of the loop.

Also note that the increment operator (++) adds 1 to the value of variable num and the result is stored back into the variable num. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement num = num + 1.
This statement prints each number in the sequence to the default standard output stream. Each printed value is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
